ticket.title: Standardize [profile.release] codegen-units across the 10 roots, measured
ticket.description: Measured, and the premise was wrong. All ten roots pin opt-level 3 + lto thin + codegen-units 1, and a stale plan claimed the single CGU cost 3x-5x release build time. Cold cargo build --release -p outfeed-cli with RUSTC_WRAPPER cleared (sccache reported 0 compile requests, proving the bypass) and target/release removed between runs, macOS 12.7.6 x86_64, cargo 1.99.1, sequential: codegen-units = 1 gave 395.58 s and 9,371,408 B; default 16 gave 398.03 s and 11,099,512 B (+18.4% binary). Wall time is dominated by dependency codegen plus the thin-LTO link, not per-crate CGU splitting, so the change would have bought 0.6% (inside noise) for 1.7 MB. Decision: keep codegen-units = 1 in all ten roots, no code change; numbers recorded in CONTRIBUTING.md section 1.5 and in the closing commit. Re-test only if lto moves to fat or false, or a binary changes shape materially.
acceptance_criteria: Cold release build of outfeed-cli timed with RUSTC_WRAPPER empty for codegen-units = 1 and 16, plus binary size for both
Numbers recorded in the commit, on this ticket and in a durable doc (CONTRIBUTING.md or PERF.md)
Every one of the 10 roots ends on the same [profile.release] without silently diverging

verification_receipt.summary: codegen-units 1: 395.58 s / 9,371,408 B; default 16: 398.03 s / 11,099,512 B (+18.4%); RUSTC_WRAPPER cleared with sccache at 0 compile requests; decision: keep the pin in all ten roots, numbers in CONTRIBUTING 1.5

task.title: Standardize [profile.release] codegen-units across the 10 roots, measured
task.description: All ten root manifests pin opt-level = 3, lto = thin and codegen-units = 1, which serializes codegen per crate. GB-131 plan asserted a 3x-5x release slowdown but nothing was ever timed, so this ticket exists to measure before changing anything (law 12): cold release build of outfeed-cli with RUSTC_WRAPPER cleared, codegen-units = 1 versus the default 16, same machine, sequential, recording wall time and final binary size. A worse runtime is a real result too - if the trade is bad, keep 1 for tagged releases via a dedicated release-dist profile and let local release builds use the default.
